output.summary: A highly poisonous herbaceous flowering plant native to Europe, North Africa, Central Asia and the Mediterranean region, poison hemlock usually grows as a biennial. Its hollow stems are often purple-spotted, and all parts can be poisonous, with toxicity varying by age, plant part and growing conditions.
output.edibilityNote: In high mountain Georgia, leaves were historically eaten in spring after careful cooking, often with several changes of water; the practice had largely died out.
